lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the cinema makes its real money where the studio gets *nothing*: the snack counter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One cinema owner said the corn costs about eight cents and the tub ninety two, so a dollar in all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Of every snack dollar, the food and cups cost about eighteen cents, and the cinema *keeps* eighty two.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That same owner even pipes the popcorn *smell* into the room where the film plays.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In opening week, the cinema keeps about eight dollars twenty from a bucket, but three forty from a ticket.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In 2025, the average visitor to America's biggest chain spent about eight dollars and fifty seven cents on snacks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You meet the same trick at home, where the printer is cheap and the ink is not.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So *share* one bucket between two, and it costs you five dollars each.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because the ticket pays for the movie, but the popcorn pays for the cinema.
